rebuild_server.usage_note: Retry a failed server build. Requires project_id in addition to server_id -- an incomplete call is rejected by input validation, not silently accepted. Used both for direct retries after a transient core failure (connection drop, gateway timeout, boot-time device error) and after a resync confirms the underlying resource's real state now matches what the build expects. Returns 202 Accepted with no response body -- this only sends the rebuild request, it does not wait for or report completion. The CMP admin-v2 API has no server-status GET to poll; confirm the outcome via cmp-logs (search for a follow-up server_creator log line for the same execution_id) rather than treating the 202 as success. (The legacy v1 admin-api's equivalent, admin_api_servers_recreate, is pollable instead -- its server detail GET reports a power_state that goes 'pending' then 'running'; see that operation's annotation if v1 is in play.)
preconditions: if root cause was a state-drift (volume/port status mismatch), resync that resource first

server_evacuate.usage_note: Move a single server off its current compute host onto another with capacity.

evacuate_compute_node.usage_note: Move every server off a compute host at once. Broad blast radius -- affects every workload on the host, not just the one under investigation.

delete_server.usage_note: Admin-delete a server. Standard deletion refuses a server in the pending state; when ALLOW_DELETE_PENDING_SERVER is enabled, a pending server can be force-deleted -- the delete retries against core up to FORCE_DELETE_CORE_RETRIES times, then the server is removed from the CMP database regardless of the result, and resources never created on core are cleaned up too.

schedule_delete_server.usage_note: Schedule a server for deletion rather than deleting it immediately.

list_compute_nodes.usage_note: Returns real per-host capacity (vcpus/ram/disk total and used, running_vms). Check this before deciding a capacity-exhaustion hypothesis (e.g. NoValidHost) is correct, and to find a host with headroom before an evacuate.

associate_floating_ip.usage_note: Claims the floating IP in the CMP database first, then schedules an async FloatingIPBindingSyncEvent that does the real binding on core afterward. This DB-first, core-second sequencing is the structural reason state drift exists -- if the sync event fails or races, CMP's record and core's real state can disagree from this point on.

cancel_scan.usage_note: Stops an in-progress security scan (see create_scan/launch_scan) before it completes. No effect on the target hosts/IPs beyond ending the scan traffic.

change_password_server.usage_note: Resets the server's admin/root password. The previous password stops working immediately -- confirm the new credential will actually reach whoever needs it before calling this.

clone_server.usage_note: Creates 1-5 new servers (quantity, max 5) as copies of server_id. Each clone is a new billable resource; this does not modify or stop the source server.

console_server.usage_note: Requests a console access URL/token for the server -- does not change server state despite being a POST. Safe to call freely for out-of-band access when a server is unresponsive to normal management calls.

create_aggregate.usage_note: Creates a host-aggregate scheduling group (a named pool of compute hosts, e.g. for flavor/AZ pinning). Affects where future servers get scheduled; does not move or affect already-running servers.

create_custom_image.usage_note: Creates a custom disk image from an existing volume (volume_id). Unlike the other custom-image operations, this one is implemented per the spec -- get/list/update/delete_custom_image are marked Not Implemented there.

create_scan.usage_note: Defines a security scan against a list of target_ips using a scan template_id -- creates the scan record but does not start it (see launch_scan). Confirm target_ips are the intended, authorized hosts before creating.

create_server_action_schedule.usage_note: Schedules a future, unattended start/stop/delete action on server_id (once/daily/weekly/monthly). Treat as high-risk whenever action='delete' is being scheduled -- approving this creates a future deletion with no further confirmation at execution time. Always check the action value before approving.

create_template.usage_note: Defines a reusable scan configuration template referenced by create_scan's template_id. No effect on any running infrastructure by itself.

delete_aggregate.usage_note: Deletes a host-aggregate scheduling group definition. Does not affect servers already running on the hosts in that aggregate -- only affects future scheduling decisions that referenced it.

delete_custom_image.usage_note: Per the CMP API spec, this operation is marked Not Implemented on the backend -- expect it to fail or return a stub response rather than actually deleting anything.

delete_scan.usage_note: Deletes a scan record (and its results). Does not affect the previously-scanned target hosts.

delete_server_action_schedule.usage_note: Removes a scheduled future server action before it runs. If the schedule's action was 'delete', this is what prevents that unattended deletion from happening -- confirm you're removing the intended schedule_id.

delete_template.usage_note: Deletes a reusable scan template. Does not affect scans already created from it.

disable_compute_node.usage_note: Stops new servers from being scheduled onto this compute host. UNVERIFIED whether this affects servers already running on the host for this CMP deployment -- vanilla OpenStack semantics say no (future scheduling only). See mcp_servers/annotations/UNVERIFIED.md.

disassociate_floating_ip.usage_note: Releases the floating IP's binding to this server in the CMP database, then schedules an async unbind on core -- same DB-first, core-second sequencing as associate_floating_ip, with the same state-drift risk if the sync event fails or races.

enable_compute_node.usage_note: Resumes scheduling new servers onto this compute host after it was disabled. Companion to disable_compute_node -- purely additive, doesn't stop or move anything.

get_aggregate.usage_note: Detail for one host-aggregate scheduling group -- membership (which compute hosts belong to it) and metadata. Check this when a scheduling/affinity failure might be aggregate-related (e.g. a server's flavor/image requires an aggregate the target host isn't a member of).

get_compute_node.usage_note: Full detail for one compute host -- capacity, status, and running VM count. Check this before deciding a capacity-exhaustion hypothesis (e.g. NoValidHost) is correct for a specific host, or to confirm a host's current status/health.

get_custom_image.usage_note: Per the CMP API spec, this operation is marked Not Implemented on the backend.

get_scan.usage_note: Detail and status for one security scan.

get_server_action_schedule.usage_note: Detail for one scheduled server action -- check the action field (start/stop/delete) before relying on delete_server_action_schedule or update_server_action_schedule decisions.

get_server_compute_node.usage_note: Which compute host a server is currently running on -- placement only, not the host's own capacity/status (see get_compute_node for that). Useful for correlating a server-level symptom with a specific host.

get_template.usage_note: Detail for one reusable scan template.

launch_scan.usage_note: Starts actual scan traffic against the scan's target_ips. This generates real network traffic against those targets and may trigger security alerting on the receiving side if they're not expecting it.

list_custom_images.usage_note: Per the CMP API spec, this operation is marked Not Implemented on the backend.

list_server_action_schedules.usage_note: All scheduled server actions -- check the action field on entries before assuming a schedule is benign, since it can be a pending delete.

list_server_types.usage_note: Available server flavors/types for building or resizing a server.

partial_update_custom_image.usage_note: Per the CMP API spec, this operation is marked Not Implemented on the backend -- expect it to fail or return a stub response.

reboot_server.usage_note: Reboots the server -- brief downtime while it restarts. Confirm this is the intended target before calling.

rescue_server.usage_note: Boots the server into rescue mode (a temporary recovery image with the original disk attached) -- used to repair a server that won't boot normally. The server is unavailable for its normal workload while rescued; call unrescue_server to return it to normal operation.

resize_server.usage_note: Changes the server's flavor (CPU/RAM/disk), either to a predefined flavor (by id) or a custom one (family/vcpus/ram/...). UNVERIFIED whether this applies immediately with a reboot or some other mechanism -- there is no separate confirm_resize/revert_resize operation in this API, unlike vanilla OpenStack's two-phase resize. See mcp_servers/annotations/UNVERIFIED.md; treat as potentially disruptive until confirmed.

scan_send_mail.usage_note: Emails scan results to mail_recipients (and bcc_emails). No infrastructure impact -- confirm the recipient list is correct before sending, since scan results may include internal IP/network details.

set_down_compute_node.usage_note: Force-marks a compute host as down, typically as a precursor to evacuate_compute_node when a host has actually failed. UNVERIFIED blast radius on already-running VMs for this CMP deployment -- see mcp_servers/annotations/UNVERIFIED.md. Don't call this on a host that's actually healthy.

stop_server.usage_note: Stops the server -- it becomes unavailable until start_server (or another start) is called. Confirm this is the intended target before calling; stopping the wrong server is a self-inflicted outage.

unrescue_server.usage_note: Returns a rescued server (see rescue_server) to normal boot from its own disk.

unset_down_compute_node.usage_note: Clears the forced-down state set by set_down_compute_node once the host is confirmed healthy again.

update_aggregate.usage_note: Updates a host-aggregate's own metadata (name, availability zone). Use update_aggregate_hosts to change which hosts belong to it.

update_aggregate_hosts.usage_note: Changes which compute hosts belong to this aggregate. Affects future scheduling against this aggregate, not servers already running.

update_aggregate_metadata.usage_note: Updates key/value metadata on a host-aggregate (used for scheduler filters like flavor pinning).

update_server_action_schedule.usage_note: Modifies an existing scheduled server action. Same caution as create_server_action_schedule -- check the resulting action value (existing or newly set) before approving, since this can turn an existing schedule into a future unattended delete.

update_server_bandwidth.usage_note: Changes the server's network bandwidth allocation. Not destructive, but can affect application performance if set too low.
